title: Which class had the most students absent?
description: The bars of the absent-students graph are compared by height to find the class with the most students absent. Keeko's doubt, that the height of the tallest bar is the answer, is checked against what the question asks for.
teaching_notes: One idea: the tallest bar shows the largest number, and its label names the answer when the question asks for the class. Watch for students who give the height of the bar instead of the class.

source: In which class were the maximum number of students absent? ___
video_script.why: The child learns to find the largest value by the tallest bar and to read the label under it.
video_script.substitution: Look along all the bars, pick the tallest, and read the class under it.
video_script.anchor: the bar graph of students absent in each class, with one unit of length for one student
video_script.wrong_answer: the answer is seven, because the tallest bar reaches seven
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko gives the height of the tallest bar. The height is how many students were absent, but the question asks which class.
video_script.payoff_line: Class eight had the most students absent

names.{{NAME_5}}: collects the absent-students data and makes the pictograph and bar graph

hold_back: Class 8 had the most students absent
maths_rules: the tallest bar is the bar of Class 8, which reaches the line marked 7
the next tallest bars are Class 2 and Class 7, each 5; 7 is more than 5
video_script.design: One idea: the tallest bar shows the largest value and the label under it is the answer. The graph stays on the board all video and a flat ruler slides across the bar tops.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the bar graph of students absent in each class, Class 1 to Class 8, with the words 1 unit length = 1 student

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.graph: the bar graph of students absent in each class appears
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the whole row of bars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the same bar graph.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>{{NAME_5}} drew a bar for the students absent in each of eight classes.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>In which class were the most students absent? How can the bars tell us?

beats.on_screen: the bar graph stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two bars side by side, the bar of Class 1 reaching 3 and the bar of Class 2 reaching 5; the taller one is ticked

marks.two: the bars of Class 1 and Class 2 stand side by side
marks.taller: the taller bar of Class 2 is ticked
marks.more: the words taller bar, bigger number appear

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Look at two bars. The bar of Class one reaches three, and the bar of Class two reaches five.
<bookmark mark='taller'/>The taller bar belongs to Class two.
<bookmark mark='more'/>A taller bar always means a bigger number, so more students were absent in Class two.

beats.on_screen: Given: the bar graph of students absent in each class; 1 unit length = 1 student

marks.given: the words the bar graph of students absent in each class are written
marks.unit: the words 1 unit length = 1 student are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the graph shows the students absent in each class.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>One unit of length stands for one student.

beats.on_screen: To find: the class with the maximum number of students absent

marks.find: the words the class with the most students absent are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the class with the most students absent.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: a flat ruler slides along the tops of all 8 bars and stops at the highest top

marks.look: all eight bars are lit together
marks.ruler: a flat ruler slides along the tops of the bars

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Step one, look at all eight bars together, because we must compare every one.
<bookmark mark='ruler'/>Slide your eyes along the tops of the bars and stop at the highest top.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the tallest bar is lit; it reaches the line marked 7; the next tallest bars reach 5

marks.seven: the top of the tallest bar is shown at the line marked 7
marks.five: two other bars are shown reaching only 5

narration: <bookmark mark='tall'/>Step two, pick the tallest bar, because it shows the biggest number.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>It reaches the line marked seven.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The next tallest bars reach only five, so seven is the largest.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the label under the tallest bar: Class 8

marks.label: the label under the tallest bar is circled
marks.name: the label Class 8 is written beside the bar

narration: <bookmark mark='label'/>Step three, read the label under that bar, because the question asks which class.
<bookmark mark='name'/>The label says Class eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Class 8 had the most students absent
narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Class eight had the most students absent.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bar graph
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says the answer is 7; the height 7 is tagged how many students; the label Class 8 is tagged which class; the bubble is struck through

marks.height: the height 7 is tagged how many students
marks.which: the label is tagged which class and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is seven, because the tallest bar reaches seven.
<bookmark mark='height'/>But seven tells us how many students were absent.
<bookmark mark='which'/>The question asks which class, so the answer is the label under the bar.
